name: Cyclic Learning Rate Tradeoff Benchmark
description: Benchmarking the tradeoff between neural network accuracy and training time is computationally expensive. Here we show how a multiplicative cyclic learning rate schedule can be used to construct a tradeoff curve in a single training run. We generate cyclic tradeoff curves for combinations of training methods such as Blurpool, Channels Last, Label Smoothing and MixUp, and highlight how these cyclic tradeoff curves can be used to evaluate the effects of algorithmic choices on network training efficiency.
evaluation_method: accuracy vs. training_time tradeoff (e.g., peak accuracy, time-to-accuracy, and cyclic tradeoff curves)
general_score_metric: accuracy vs. training_time tradeoff (e.g., time-to-target-accuracy, peak accuracy at given compute)
reputation: A focused research benchmark/protocol (from 2206.00832) used in studies of training efficiency; moderately cited but not a broadly standardized benchmark.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark and protocol rather than a fixed dataset; computationally expensive to run full experiments; results depend on implementation details (optimizer, hardware, augmentation), so reproducibility requires careful control.
